svg.aria-label: Spinifex across three OCI instances: all three sit inside the VCN public subnet 10.200.0.0/23, one per fault domain. Each carries a primary VNIC for the cluster mesh and a br-wan secondary VNIC holding its reserved public addresses, its own iSCSI block volume, and its share of the guests. Geneve, NATS JetStream, predastore erasure coding and the OVN raft join them east-west.
svg.text: three fault domains · one region · one API endpoint
Three OCI instances, redundant multi-node install
Guest-to-guest traffic rides Geneve between the nodes' primary VNICs — it never leaves the subnet and never touches br-wan.
A guest that moves takes its address with it.
The reserved public IP follows the secondary private IP to whichever node's br-wan the guest lands on — the tenant sees no change.
Three nodes is the smallest cluster that tolerates losing one: NATS JetStream keeps quorum, predastore RS(2,1)
keeps the data readable, and the OVN Northbound raft keeps a leader. One node per fault domain is what makes that real.
